subject: Re: Brightline POC — scope redesign & acceptance criteria (next steps)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.health>; Tom Lawson <tlawson@brightline.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Brightline call recap + proposed POC plan (success criteria & owners)

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed next step to get the POC scoped and kickoff-ready. Please confirm or flag changes.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary goal: reduce manual triage time for inbound member messages and automate intent routing for claims/refund/appeals.
- Key workflows to test in POC: intent classification & redirecting to correct queue; extract structured fields for refund requests (amount, date, order id); conversational fallbacks to triage agents.

Proposed POC scope (4 weeks, two sprints)
- Week 0 (prep): data ingest + schema mapping (Brightline provides 500 sample messages and label guidance).
- Sprint 1: intent classification + routing (target 85% precision on routing for top 5 intents).
- Sprint 2: refund extraction pipeline + integration with ticketing (target 80% exact-match on amount & order id).

Success criteria (please confirm):
- Intent routing: >=85% precision & >=75% recall on the labeled test set.
- Refund extraction: >=80% field-level accuracy for amount and order id.
- Latency: median inference latency <150ms for 512 token prompt at 95th percentile.
- Ops: sample end-to-end flow executed by customer within test environment and validated by success checklist.

Ownership & next steps
- Brightline: provide sample dataset + a short acceptance checklist (who will validate).
- Redwood: deliver model endpoints, integration adapter for ticketing, weekly demo & interim metrics.
- Proposed kickoff: Monday Nov 23 — we can shift if you need additional prep.

Attachments: poc-success-matrix.xlsx (draft acceptance checklist)

If this looks right, I’ll lock timelines and loop in engineering (Monica + Ben) to confirm capacity.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwoodai.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.health>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Tom Lawson <tlawson@brightline.health>, Brightline Health Procurement <procurement@brightline.health>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightline call recap + proposed POC plan (success criteria & owners)

Thanks Priyom — this is a clear summary, appreciate it. A couple of adjustments from our side after we aligned with ops: 

1) Add one mid-trial use case: refund intent triage + auto-draft of refund recommendation (the recommendation is a short structured text block our agents can copy into the ticket). We want to validate quality of the recommendation text (human grade: >80% accept rate in a small blind review).
2) Slightly change the success criteria: prefer precision thresholds to be presented with a short confidence band (e.g., 85% +/- 3%). We’ll accept a small degradation if the recommendation accept rate is >80%.
3) Timeline: we can still do the kickoff Nov 23 but will need two additional weeks on data curation — can you accommodate shifting the end date by +2 weeks?

I’ve attached our internal evaluation plan (brightline-eval-plan-v2.xlsx) which includes the blind review procedure and the list of top ticket categories. Also looping procurement for contract/NDAs.

On the resource side, if adding the recommendation generation increases model cost, please provide an estimate of incremental GPU hours and any recommended quantization / model variant that keeps latency targets.

Appreciate it — Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Member Ops | Brightline Health
sarah@brightline.health

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.health>, Tom Lawson <tlawson@brightline.health>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Brightline call recap + proposed POC plan — customer asks to add recommendation generation (needs impact & owners)

Team — forwarding Sarah’s note. Brightline wants to: (A) add a recommendation-generation use case mid-trial (short structured text recommendations to paste into tickets) and (B) extend the POC by two weeks to allow for data curation and their blind review.

Questions / asks for engineering + solutions:
- Feasibility: can we add the recommendation-generation step (light-generation -> templated output) within the POC window if we extend +2 weeks?
- Impact: estimate incremental GPU usage and whether we can meet the latency SLOs (median <150ms at p95) with a recommended quantized variant.
- Owners: who on infra/dev should own the extraction->generation adapter and the demo for blind-review?

Prelim notes: from the call, the customer has ~500 labeled messages. The blind review requires us to surface recommendation text for 100 blind samples. If we run a smaller batch size for generation to keep quality, we may need ~10–15 extra GPU hours/week during sprint 2 (rough estimate).

Please reply with a short answer (owner + estimate + any blocker) so I can respond to Sarah and confirm new timeline and sign-off.

Thanks — Priyom

[attachment: brightline-eval-plan-v2.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodai.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.health>, Tom Lawson <tlawson@brightline.health>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Brightline call recap + proposed POC plan — customer asks to add recommendation generation (needs impact & owners)

Got it — fyi assigning engineering owner: Lukas Meyer will own the adapter and demo. Monica can own validation checklist and Naomi will coordinate demo scheduling with Brightline.

Quick estimates:
- Timeline: +2 weeks is fine; will keep kickoff Nov 23 but shift internal sprint end to Dec 18 (new end date).
- Compute: approx +12 GPU hours/week during Sprint 2 for low-latency generation at a 13B quantized FP16/INT8 mix.
- Latency: with the quantized 13B variant we should hit p95 ~140–160ms depending on network; we will target configuration that biases latency under 150ms for typical 512-token prompts.
- Risk: blind review accept-rate is content-dependent; recommend we add a small prompt engineering sprint early in Sprint 2 and include 50-shot tuning with their 100 blind samples.

Links: integration test harness (internal): https://internal.redwood/test-harness/BR-4421

I’ll add Lukas to the thread and loop in infra for capacity.

Ben Carter
